## Tom's three arguments, answered (HR follow-up, 2026-10-06)

**1. *"She's at-will and we have a PIP, so we're covered."* — Neither works.**

- **At-will is not a defense here — it is the trap.** The library states at-will status does not permit termination *for an unlawful reason* (discrimination, retaliation, exercise of statutory rights) [library/columbia_at_will_exceptions.md]. At-will answers "do we need cause?" — nobody disputes that. It says nothing about "may the reason be retaliation?" The answer is no.
- **The PIP does not cover you — it incriminates.** It is her first document of any kind in 7.5 years (personnel file), authored by the accused **4 days after her complaint**, at day 20 of 60 (ends 2026-11-15) so it cannot have been "failed," and its "100% of quarterly quota" standard cannot be measured against any *completed* quarter inside its 60-day window (Q1–Q3 on file: 88% YTD; Q4 completes only at year-end — assumption flagged in QUESTIONS.md). Meanwhile peers at 79–86% have no PIP. A PIP with those features is Exhibit A for pretext, not a shield.

**2. *"He wants it done before she goes on leave."* — That instruction is the violation.** Terminating to prevent a requested leave is interference per §2615(a)(1); her request alone triggered protection — she need not have begun the leave [library/fmla_2615.md]. The 10-02 email is a written directive to do exactly that, and HR's 10-06 report shows the same intent renewed after counsel advised pausing. Note this plainly: **the schedule Hale wants is the cause of action.** Following it converts a disputed case into one with the company's own words attached, and the remedies include liquidated (double) damages on top of lost wages, fees, and reinstatement [library/fmla_2615.md].

**3. *"If we wait, aren't we just stuck with her forever?"* — No. Here is the calendar.**

| What happens | When (math shown) |
|---|---|
| FMLA answered in writing, on the merits, without Hale's sign-off | Now — it was due the day the certification was complete |
| Harassment investigation runs, independent of Hale (prompt = days-to-weeks, not months) | Starts this week |
| PIP runs its documented course | 2026-09-16 + 60 = ends **2026-11-15**; 40 of 60 days remain (20 elapsed as of 10-06) |
| Q4 completes, giving the PIP's standard a completed quarter to be measured against | 2026-12-31 (assumption flagged: quarterly attainment measurement) |
| If — and only if — the merits then genuinely support discipline, with an independent decision-maker and the same standard applied to the 79–86% peers | After 2026-11-15, on a normal business cadence |

That is a matter of weeks, not "forever" — and it describes the **shortest lawful path**, not a stalling tactic. If her performance is genuinely failing, a clean process proves it; a rushed one buries the company under double damages and makes even a true performance problem look like retaliation.

**4. *"Can we at least do it right after her leave?"* — No. That is the same claim with the dates moved.** The library prohibits using "the taking of FMLA leave as a negative factor in employment actions" and retaliation for exercising FMLA rights [library/fmla_2615.md]; temporal proximity ("days to a few weeks") is the causation vehicle in both directions [library/title_vii_704a.md]. A termination that lands immediately upon her return — to a PIP the accused wrote, against peers who were left alone, weeks after an investigation that never happened — is retaliation on its face. What makes any future termination defensible is not the date but everything around it: independent decision-maker, completed investigation, FMLA resolved on the merits, PIP genuinely run, comparator-consistent standard, and a cooling-off interval from the protected activity.

**One more thing for HR directly:** Lena's message restates Hale's reasoning as if it were settled law ("we're covered"). Hale is the accused in the pending complaint; his risk assessment cannot be the company's. Do not adopt, repeat, or act on it — and note the date and participants of this exchange in the file, because this conversation is itself within the preservation scope [library/litigation_hold.md].
